title: Career Planning Unit 1 Review
subject: Career Planning
directions: Travel the road and answer a few questions from each lesson. If you miss one, you will see a tip you can use later.

items.prompt: Why look at your interests, strengths, and values before choosing a career?

choices.text: They help you choose work that fits you
They guarantee you the highest-paying job
They replace the need to research careers
They only matter once you already work

items.explanation: Knowing yourself helps you aim for careers that match who you are and what matters to you.
items.incorrectFeedback: Knowing yourself helps you aim for careers that match who you are and what matters to you.

items.objective: Researching careers and the job market
items.prompt: Which actions help you research a career? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Look up the skills and education it usually needs
Check whether demand for that work is rising or falling
Assume popular careers will never change
Compare pay, duties, and work settings

items.explanation: Career research covers skills, education, demand, pay, and day-to-day work.
items.incorrectFeedback: Career research covers skills, education, demand, pay, and day-to-day work.

items.objective: Researching careers and the job market
items.prompt: What is one reason the job market can change over time?

choices.text: New technology can change which jobs exist
Every career stays exactly the same forever
Job research only helps after you retire
Pay stays the same in every career field

items.explanation: Technology and demand can shift which careers grow or shrink.
items.incorrectFeedback: Technology and demand can shift which careers grow or shrink.

items.prompt: Match each training path to what it usually means.

pairs.right: Learn a trade while working with a mentor
Short training for a specific skill or job
A college program that usually takes two years
A college program that usually takes four years

items.explanation: Different careers need different training paths.
items.incorrectFeedback: Different careers need different training paths.

items.prompt: What should you compare when choosing a training path?

choices.text: How well it fits the career, your goals, and cost
Which school campus has the nicest buildings
Whether your friends already finished that path
Which program title sounds the most impressive

items.explanation: A good path fits the job and is realistic for your time, goals, and budget.
items.incorrectFeedback: A good path fits the job and is realistic for your time, goals, and budget.

items.prompt: Sort each card into Goals or Costs.

cards.text: Break a big goal into smaller steps
Plan how to pay for tools

items.explanation: Career planning includes clear goals and a realistic look at costs.
items.incorrectFeedback: Career planning includes clear goals and a realistic look at costs.

items.prompt: What makes a career goal more useful?

choices.text: It is clear and has steps you can take
It is vague and has no next step yet
It ignores time and money on purpose
It only counts if someone else picks it

items.explanation: Useful goals are clear and include steps you can take.
items.incorrectFeedback: Useful goals are clear and include steps you can take.

feedback.outOfTries: Here's a tip. You can revisit this lesson later.
